summary: This standards-track document defines how to package SPIRIT IP-MR speech codec audio in RTP. It allows several frames per packet and adds redundancy for robustness against packet loss and bit errors.

eli5.summary: This is a box design for sending one company's compressed voice recordings over the internet, with extra copies to survive losses.

questions: what is the ip-mr rtp payload format
what is the ip-mr media type
subtitle: How to put scalable, loss-resistant SPIRIT IP-MR wideband speech into RTP packets.

tldr.problem: The IP-MR speech codec produces layered frames whose bits are not equally sensitive to damage, and it needs a standard way to travel in RTP while surviving packet loss.
tldr.mechanism: Each RTP payload carries a small header, a table of contents and one to four frames, optionally followed by a redundancy payload that repeats the most sensitive parts of the two previous packets.
tldr.outcome: Senders can trade bandwidth against robustness inside the packet, and gateways can drop enhancement layers without re-encoding, with no out-of-band signalling needed for the redundancy.

today: RFC 6262 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2011. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The IP-MR Codec
sections.content:
RFC 6262 specifies how to packetize speech encoded with SPIRIT IP-MR into the Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP). The format supports several frames per packet and adds redundancy for robustness against packet loss and bit errors.

IP-MR is a wideband speech codec designed for conferencing over packet-switched networks. It works on frames of 20 ms at a 16 kHz sampling rate, with a total end-to-end delay of 25 ms. It is scalable: there are 6 coding rates from 7.7 to 34.2 kbps, and a gateway can lower the bandwidth at any time without performance overhead. Each frame is a sequence of layers. The first, the base layer, is mandatory, while the enhancement layers can be safely discarded. The codec also has built-in discontinuous transmission (DTX) and comfort noise generation (CNG).

Not all bits in a base layer are equally tolerant of damage. IP-MR defines 6 sensitivity classes, 'A' to 'F'. Damage to class 'A' bits causes significant artifacts, while loss in class 'F' may not even be heard.
sections.eli5: The voice is squeezed into layers like an onion. The middle layer is needed, and the outer layers just make it sound nicer, so they can be peeled off when the road is crowded.

sections.title: The Speech Payload Header and TOC
sections.content:
The IP-MR payload has two parts, each shaped as header, table of contents (TOC) and data: one for current speech and an optional one for redundancy. The speech header is 12 bits and holds settings common to all frames in the packet.

  • T (1 bit): reserved, MUST be 0.
  • CR (3 bits): coding rate index, the top enhancement layer available. The value 7 (NO_DATA) means no speech data, which MAY be used to send only redundancy.
  • BR (3 bits): base rate index. Packets with BR = 6 or BR greater than CR MUST be discarded.
  • D (1 bit): reserved, MUST be 1.
  • A (1 bit): 1 means padding so every compressed frame starts on a byte boundary.
  • GR (2 bits): frames in the packet minus one, so the maximum is 4.
  • R (1 bit): 1 means a redundancy payload is present.

Rate indices 0 to 5 map to average bitrates of 7.7, 9.8, 14.3, 20.8, 27.9 and 34.2 kbps. Index 6 is reserved and a packet that uses it MUST be discarded. The speech TOC follows, unless CR is 7: one E bit per frame, where 0 means no speech data for that frame. The encoder sets it to 0 for silence in DTX mode, and applications MUST set it to 0 if a frame is known to be damaged.
sections.eli5: The header is a short label on the box: how many voice pieces are inside, how fancy the sound is, and whether spare copies are tucked in too.

sections.title: Using the RTP Header and Frame Data
sections.content:
The RTP header follows RFC 3550. The timestamp clock SHALL run at 16 kHz. A frame lasts 20 ms, which is 320 samples, so the timestamp increases by 320 for each consecutive frame. The marker bit SHALL be 1 when the first frame-block in the packet is the first in a talkspurt, and 0 otherwise.

The payload type is not assigned by this document. It is bound dynamically, because it expresses the payload configuration, such as basic or interleaved mode and the number of channels.

The speech data holds GR+1 compressed frames. A frame whose TOC flag is 0 has length zero. Frames start on byte boundaries only if the A bit is set, but the end of the speech payload is always byte aligned. Within a frame, the base layer is divided into sensitivity classes A to F, followed by enhancement layers. Appendix A gives a C helper routine, which MUST be used to extract sensitivity classes and enhancement layer bounds from the compressed frame.
sections.eli5: Each frame is a 20 ms slice of sound. The timestamp counts forward by the same step for every slice, so the listener can put them back in order.

sections.title: Redundancy for Packet Loss
sections.content:
When the R bit is 1, a redundancy payload follows the speech payload. It carries data for the preceding and the pre-preceding packets. Its header has two 3-bit fields, CL1 and CL2, which say how many sensitivity classes are included for each of the two earlier packets.

A CL value of 0 means none, 1 means class A only, 2 means A-B, and so on up to 6 meaning A-F. The value 7 is reserved, and a decoder MUST discard the redundancy payload if CL is 0 or 7. The BR and GR values are not repeated, so applications MUST assume they match the current packet. A redundancy TOC then gives one E bit for each frame of the two earlier packets.

Redundancy is available only if the base rates and coding rates of the earlier packets are the same as the current one. A receiver MAY use it to cover for lost packets, and it can then reconstruct the base layer of earlier packets fully (CL=6) or partly. The enhancement layers cannot be retransmitted.
sections.eli5: Every box carries small copies of the most important bits from the two boxes before it. If a box falls off the truck, the next one can patch up most of the hole.

sections.title: Congestion Control and Bandwidth
sections.content:
The general RTP congestion considerations of RFC 3550 and the audio-video profile (RFC 3551) apply. The multi-rate design offers an extra tool, since bandwidth demand can be changed by choosing a different encoding mode.

Putting more frames in each packet cuts IP/UDP/RTP header overhead, at the cost of more delay. The minimum rate is set by the BR field and can be as low as 7.7 kbps. Quality depends on the coding rate rather than the base rate, so it is NOT RECOMMENDED to use high BR values for real-time communications.

Applications MAY use redundancy to fight packet loss, but a gateway may drop coding layers or redundancy bits to reduce the rate. For that reason it is NOT RECOMMENDED to raise the total bitrate when adding redundancy in response to loss.
sections.eli5: If the road gets crowded, you can send smaller boxes. Do not send extra spare copies when the road is already jammed, because that makes it worse.

sections.title: Security and Session Parameters
sections.content:
The packets are subject to the security considerations of RFC 3550 and the applicable RTP profile. The main concerns are confidentiality, integrity and source authenticity. The RFC says a single mechanism is not sufficient because the right choice depends on the application, transport and signalling, but recommends SRTP (RFC 3711) if suitable. IPsec and TLS (for RTP over TCP) are also mentioned. The format does not cause significant non-uniformity in receiver computation, so it is unlikely to pose a denial-of-service threat from pathological data.

The media type is audio/ip-mr_v2.5. The subtype name reflects an internal codec version that was later accepted as final, and 'IP-MR' and 'IP-MR v2.5' are now synonyms. The only optional parameter is ptime, with allowed values 20, 40, 60 and 80 milliseconds. In SDP, the clock rate in a=rtpmap MUST be 16000.
sections.eli5: To keep the voice private and prevent tampering, you use the usual safe-delivery tools for RTP. The label for this kind of audio is ip-mr_v2.5.
